paragraphs: Instructor: Scott Wright
Pre-Quarter Assignment: Cemetery Composition

This painting tells the story of a boy who wants to bring flowers to a friend who has died. Cemetery security stops him from approaching his friend's grave. He is standing in a tree, holding the flowers and trying to reach the grave.
My main focus was lighting. I used contrasts in both light and dark values and warm and cool colors to draw attention to the important parts of the scene.

This was also my first attempt to paint primarily with planes of color. I had previously relied more on lines to construct forms, so I started using larger color shapes and value relationships to organize the painting. I was still unfamiliar with the approach, which made the process challenging.
Project 1: The Lost Spaceship
I used a spaceship stranded in the desert to explore differences in scale and the contrast between the ship and its surroundings.

I tried different compositions to explore the difference in size between the ship and the character. In some thumbnails, the spaceship appears enormous and the figure very small. In others, stronger perspective emphasizes the ship's scale and the space around it.

I made nine sketches and selected the seventh, at the bottom left, for the final painting. The scene takes place in a desert canyon surrounded by rough rocks, with a spaceship made of transparent crystal in the middle.

I wanted the smooth crystal to contrast with the rough rock, while the ship's own light contrasts with the darkness of the canyon. These differences also help convey the sense that the ship and its surroundings belong to different eras.
In this project, I learned to apply the 7:2:1 principle in composition, using the proportions occupied by different visual elements to control the focal point.
Rendering rock and crystal pushed me to move beyond line-based construction and use broad shapes of light and shadow to describe volume and materials.

paragraphs: Instructor: Cyril Guichard

Boss Rush is my first bullet-hell game, developed with JavaScript and Microsoft MakeCode Arcade. I first learned about the platform through my professor. Before our group project began, I spent about a week independently making the initial version, designing and building its gameplay, art, and code myself.

My earlier experience with Scratch made the visual programming environment familiar. I continued expanding the combat systems and content afterward, turning Boss Rush into a personal project that I developed on my own.

Players face successive boss battles, dodge dense bullet patterns, and decide when to move, defend, or attack. Each boss has a signature mechanic, while its other attacks combine randomly selected main patterns with smaller sub-patterns, creating variation across repeated encounters.
Play Boss Rush - v1.0.17
Keyboard controls: Z = controller A; X = controller B. Boss Rush was designed around console-style buttons, while the browser simulator maps those buttons to keyboard keys.
Randomized Patterns and Signature Attacks

I developed a pool of main patterns and smaller sub-patterns that are randomly assigned when a boss spawns. Each boss has its own signature attack, allowing repeat encounters to vary while retaining a distinct combat identity.
LASER's regular attack sends shifting laser-projectile patterns across the arena. Players must read their trajectories and find openings while moving.
Boss Ultimates and Enraged Phases

Bosses enter the enraged phase below 30% HP, upgrading their attacks. DANMAKU specializes in dense rotating projectiles, while WALL changes the speed and reverses the direction of its ultimate attack during the enraged phase. Version 1.0.17 reduced DANMAKU's ultimate density and rotation speed while strengthening WALL's and RUSH's enraged attacks.
The summoning ultimate introduces additional enemies, turning a single-boss fight into a multi-target encounter where players must manage movement, projectiles, and summoned threats at once.

paragraphs: Instructor: Gregory Johnson
Project 1: Fire Extinguisher Modeling

I built a fire extinguisher in Autodesk 3ds Max, modeling the cylinder, valve, handle, pressure gauge, hose, and connectors separately. I used chamfers and carefully placed joints to refine the hard-surface construction, then adjusted materials and lighting to distinguish the different surfaces.
Project 2: Fox Character Sculpting

I sculpted a stylized fox in ZBrush, building the head, body, legs, and tail from large forms before refining their connections. Oversized ears and simplified proportions establish the silhouette; I checked the model from multiple angles to balance its volumes.

paragraphs: 这幅画讲的是一个男孩想给死去的朋友献花，却被墓园的安保人员拦了下来。他站在树上，手里拿着花，试图接近朋友的墓地。
我在这幅画中主要想练习光线的表现，利用明暗对比和冷暖色彩对比突出人物和场景中的重要部分。
这也是我第一次尝试以面为基础进行绘画。过去我更习惯依靠线条建立形体，这次开始使用大面积的色块和明暗关系组织画面。由于还不熟悉这种方法，绘画过程对我来说有一定难度。
我以沙漠中迷失的飞船为主题，通过构图突出飞船与人物的尺度差异和时代反差。
我尝试通过不同的构图方式比较飞船与人物的大小。有些构图让飞船显得非常巨大，人物则十分渺小；另一些构图则使用更强烈的透视关系，突出飞船的体积和空间感。
我一共绘制了九张草图，最终选择了左下角的第七张。这张画的场景位于一座沙漠峡谷中，峡谷由粗糙的岩石构成，中间则是一艘由透明晶体构成的飞船。
我希望通过晶体的光滑与岩石的粗糙形成材质对比，同时利用飞船自身发出的光线，与峡谷中的阴暗环境形成明暗对比。这些差异也能够进一步表现飞船与周围环境之间的时代感。
在这个项目中，我学习并理解了构图中的 7:2:1 原则，以及如何通过不同元素在画面中所占的比例控制视觉重点。
岩石和晶体的材质差异也促使我从线条造型转向以大面积明暗色块塑造体积。
我将《启航星》中的机械敌人“虫后生命之箱”用于课程道具设计：它以手提箱形状的机械容器保存大脑，通过神经接口控制克隆体。此次重点是机械结构、透视与材质表现。
设计包含机械臂、皮革箱体和底部双枪管。我分别处理金属与皮革的表面反射，并调整各部件的连接方式。
由于草图的透视与零件关系比较复杂，我在玛雅中制作了简化的三维模型，并以模型为参考完成最终二维画面。画中的投影也参考了三维模型，再在图像处理软件中进行绘制。这使我能够在复杂结构中维持透视关系，并集中研究不同材质的表现。

在线游玩 Boss Rush — v1.0.17
键盘操作：Z = 游戏机 A 键；X = 游戏机 B 键。 游戏原本面向游戏机操作，因此网页模拟器使用的键盘按键与游戏内的按键名称不同。

LASER 的普通激光攻击由连续变化的激光弹幕组成，玩家需要观察弹幕轨迹，在移动中寻找躲避空间。
当 Boss 的生命值低于 30%，就会进入愤怒阶段，攻击方式随之强化。 DANMAKU 擅长密集旋转弹幕；WALL 的终极攻击在愤怒阶段会改变速度并反向运动。v1.0.17 降低了 DANMAKU 终极攻击的密度与旋转速度，同时强化了 WALL 与 RUSH 的愤怒阶段攻击。
召唤怪的大招会召唤更多敌人，将原本的单体 Boss 战变成多目标战斗，迫使玩家同时处理移动、弹幕和召唤物。
RUSH 的大招会在冲出屏幕后重新锁定玩家，并改变下一次冲锋方向。
LASER 在愤怒阶段强化终极攻击，形成由大型激光球组成的密集弹幕。程序会自动填补相邻大球之间的视觉空隙，消除大球交界处的粗糙边缘，使整体光束更加连续、完整。
HYBRID DUCK 可以强化其他 Boss。它的保护球与 RUSH、WALL 等 Boss 的攻击叠加，使多 Boss 战斗形成更复杂的弹幕组合。

title: The Mimetic Braincase
description: A mechanical enemy from The Star of Embarkation, created by combining human augmentation with Legacy technology.
excerpt: The Mimetic Braincase The Mimetic Braincase is an enemy I designed for my original series, The Star of Embarkation. Its brain resides inside a mechanical container disguised as a suitcase. The hidden controller can operate multiple clones a…
paragraphs: The Mimetic Braincase

The Mimetic Braincase is an enemy I designed for my original series, The Star of Embarkation. Its brain resides inside a mechanical container disguised as a suitcase. The hidden controller can operate multiple clones at once, using their coordinated actions while keeping its actual body concealed and mobile outside the immediate fight.

The Star of Embarkation takes place after humanity escapes a collapsing Earth aboard the Embarkation Vessel and reaches an unfamiliar planet. The vessel crashes during landing, leaving behind advanced equipment and wreckage from Earth. These technological remnants are known as the Legacy. They cannot be manufactured or replicated on the new world, making them extremely valuable. The planet's native Fiber also suppresses conventional electrical and thermal technology; many Legacy devices remain unaffected, making them especially important.

The Mimetic Braincase combines Legacy technology with human augmentation. It uses this irreplaceable technology to house a transplanted human brain in a suitcase-shaped mechanical container and control cloned bodies through neural interfaces.
Prop Design and Rendering

For the course prop project, I chose this mechanically complex enemy from The Star of Embarkation to practice rendering different geometric forms and materials. Its design includes mechanical arms, a leather suitcase, and two gun barrels under the case. I focused on the metallic finish of the arms, the leather texture of the case, and the metal of the gun barrels, while trying to make the mechanical connections plausible.

The original sketch contained so many connected parts that keeping the perspective accurate became difficult. I built a simplified model in Maya to establish the component positions and perspective, then used it as reference for the final two-dimensional painting. The shadows also drew on the three-dimensional model and were rendered in Photoshop. This workflow helped me maintain the structure while concentrating on different material qualities.
The Brain and Its Clones
I took inspiration from the hive structure in Ender's Game: as long as the hidden controller survives, it can continue operating other bodies.

Neural interfaces can be implanted in different locations, including both the brain and spinal cord of the same clone. Even if a clone suffers an otherwise fatal head injury, the controller can continue directing its movements through the spinal interface. One controller can command several clones simultaneously, coordinating them in combat and effectively forming an army of one. If a clone dies, its controller still receives the information that clone acquired. This makes the system valuable for both combat and intelligence gathering.
Concealment and Connection Limits

The brain container is disguised as an ordinary suitcase that a clone can carry. Concealed mechanical legs allow it to move at high speed like a spider. Because of this mobility, the small container can conceal itself underground, in grass, or high in trees, far from the center of a fight. In a complex environment, a searcher would find it almost impossible to locate without a way to determine its position first.

paragraphs: 《虫后生命之箱》是我为原创《启航星》系列设计的敌人。它将大脑转移到一个伪装成手提箱的机械容器中，由隐藏在战场外的本体同时操控多个克隆体。它的威胁来自克隆体之间的协作，真正的本体则依靠伪装和高速移动避开追捕。
《启航星》的故事发生在人类逃离濒临毁灭的地球，乘坐启航舰抵达一颗陌生行星之后。启航舰在降落时坠毁，留下了一批来自地球的高科技设备和残骸。这些技术遗物被称为“遗产”，由于无法在启航星重新生产或复制，因此十分珍贵。当地的“纤维”还会抑制人类惯用的电力与热能技术，许多不受纤维影响的遗产因此更加重要。
虫后生命之箱就是利用“遗产”技术与人体组合改造的产物。 它借助这些无法复制的地球技术，将人的大脑移植到手提箱形状的机械容器内，再通过神经接口远程控制多个克隆体。
在课程道具作业中，我选择把《启航星》系列里的这个敌人制作成机械设计图，主要练习不同几何体和材料的渲染。它包含机械臂、皮革箱体与箱体下方的两根枪管，我想突出机械臂的金属质感、箱包的皮革质感和枪管的金属表面，同时尽可能设计合理的机械连接结构。
由于草图的透视与零件关系比较复杂，我在玛雅中制作了简化的三维模型，并以模型为参考完成最终二维画面。画中的投影也参考了三维模型，再在图像处理软件中进行绘制。这使我能够在复杂结构中维持透视关系，并集中研究不同材质的表现。
控制方式的灵感来自《安德的游戏》中虫族首领与虫群的关系：只要隐藏的真正本体没有被击败，敌人就可以继续操控其他身体。
神经接口可以植入克隆体不同部位，例如同时植入大脑与脊髓。即使克隆体的头部遭受正常意义上的致命伤，也可以通过脊髓中的神经接口继续操控克隆体行动。一个本体可以同时操控多个克隆体，让它们在战斗中协同配合，甚至达到一人成军的效果。克隆体死亡后，本体也能获得相关信息，因此这种控制方式在战斗与情报收集方面都具有优势。
容器平时看起来是一只普通手提箱，可以由克隆体随身携带。它还隐藏着能够像蜘蛛一样高速移动的机械足。隐藏式机械足让它拥有很强的移动与逃亡能力，能够藏在地下、草丛、树顶等难以想到的位置。由于它体积小、隐蔽性强，在复杂环境中，如果无法先通过某种方法确定手提箱的具体位置，搜寻者几乎不可能直接找到本体。
这套系统有一项限制：克隆体与手提箱之间的连接范围有限，连接区域是以手提箱为圆心的一个圆。所有克隆体都必须保持连接才能维持行动。出于避免黑客攻击的设定，克隆体断线后也无法自行重新连接。本体虽然具有很强的逃亡能力，却仍然需要尽力使珍贵的克隆体维持在连接范围之内。
克隆体负责围攻和收集情报，本体则隐藏在战场外。搜寻者可以利用它们必须维持连接的限制，反推本体的位置。
搜寻者首先需要发现多个克隆体由同一个隐藏的本体控制。接着观察克隆体的行动，发现它们始终受到一个连接范围的限制。但即使知道存在连接边界，仍然无法直接确定圆形范围的半径和圆心。我设计了一种利用几何关系寻找本体的方法，并画了五张原理图展示这一过程。

paragraphs: The Rift Within the Embarkation Plan

Dyson and Lucian once shared the same ideals and worked together on the Embarkation Plan. Its emblem represents both those shared ambitions and the relationship they once had. Over time, their ideas about the future came into conflict.
Lucian wants to destroy the elves through war. In the storyboard adaptation of this scene, he points a gun at a map to express that intention. Their opposing beliefs eventually drive them apart.

In the planned story of The Star of Embarkation, both believe that they alone truly represent the Embarkation Plan. Each holds to their own understanding of its original ideals. Even after they part ways, neither wants to surrender the emblem of the plan. Their conflicting claims to the same ideals are central to the dispute.

I adapted this story into a six-panel storyboard, reducing nine sketches to six and ending with Dyson leaving and discarding the emblem. That final gesture belongs only to the coursework adaptation; in the main story, neither Dyson nor Lucian gives up the emblem.

title: The Forerunners
description: Character design: The Forerunners. Exploration, Creation, Courage. Explore the unknown, create possibility, and fight for humanity's future in desperate times.
excerpt: The Forerunners: Exploration, Creation, Courage. Around 2070, war and ecological collapse pushed Earth toward the end of civilization. To keep humanity alive, a group of survivors secretly launched The Embarkation Plan. Its aim was desperat…
paragraphs: The Forerunners: Exploration, Creation, Courage.

Around 2070, war and ecological collapse pushed Earth toward the end of civilization. To keep humanity alive, a group of survivors secretly launched The Embarkation Plan. Its aim was desperate: build the Embarkation Vessel and leave the Solar System through still-immature wormhole technology. The odds were almost hopeless, but the plan succeeded. The vessel crossed the wormhole and, after years of flight, reached an unfamiliar planet. It crashed on landing; about ten thousand survived, rescued by the planet's Sylphs. Humanity named this world The Star of Embarkation. The five leaders turned a nearly impossible escape into reality, earning immense prestige among the first survivors. Together, they came to be called — The Forerunners.

Dyson was the plan's chief engineer, leading the vessel's design, coordination, and hardware architecture. He fused Seth's core technology with Linnea's life-support system, turning separate fields into one finished work of engineering — the Embarkation Vessel. He demanded uncompromising quality in design and construction, yet remained warm, lively, and able to ease the pressure of long construction with humor. His precision and bright presence made him one of the plan's most charismatic leaders.

Seth was the plan's core physicist, leading key research and experimental wormhole development. After the vessel was built, he remained in charge of theory, route calculation, and navigation. Calm and terse, he trusted calculation, evidence, and logic. Once convinced, he rarely changed course. That stubbornness carried him through years of difficult research, and made him unyielding in disagreement. The wormhole was the technology the plan depended on; in time, it became the plan's symbol and even its emblem. Most ordinary members could not truly understand Seth's work and kept their distance, but everyone knew humanity's departure from the Solar System was tied to this silent physicist.
Lucian the Politician

Before the Embarkation Vessel was finished, it had already become something worth going to war over on a dying Earth. The engineers faced more than technical problems: warlords, panic, resource conflict, and a social order nearing collapse. Lucian handled all of it.

Lucian was the plan's politician. During construction, he led military forces against warlords trying to seize the vessel, while keeping the construction system running through war, scarcity, and prolonged psychological strain. After departure, he continued to manage society aboard the ship. Confident and responsible, he organized people, set clear goals, and made quick decisions in crisis. He gave people a sense of security the apocalypse had never offered. The trust he earned later became an important foundation of his political power.

Linnea was the plan's biologist, leading medicine, life support, and ecological cycle design. The Embarkation Vessel could not carry unlimited air, water, or food; the endurance of its ecology determined how long it could fly. Linnea was one of the few technical leaders whose work touched life itself. She had deep specialist training, but no technocrat's manner. Even at the plan's most intense moments, she remained gentle and open.

The plan needed resources far beyond an ordinary spacecraft. By then, Earth's economic, industrial, and supply systems were collapsing in war. Weapons, equipment, materials, and daily supplies still had to arrive; without them, even the best design stayed on paper. Hilda was the plan's economist, securing weapons, materials, and supplies for construction, then managing production and allocation during the voyage. Pragmatic and independent, she had a strong instinct for exploration. She read situations well and knew when to advance or retreat among competing interests. Her tact let her move among shifting parties; her judgment kept her from trusting any one method, channel, or relationship forever. Ordinary members understood her less directly than Lucian, and her work had no clear symbol l…

The five Forerunners represented engineering, science, order, life, and resources. Only with every one of these links could the Embarkation Vessel be built, leave Earth, complete its long voyage, and let humanity rebuild society in another world. Without any one of them, none of it could have happened. To the first survivors, these names came from living memory: they had carried humanity from the end of an old civilization to the beginning of a new one.

paragraphs: 先行者：探索、创造、勇敢。探索未知，创造可能，在绝境中为人类文明争取未来。

2070年前后，战争与生态崩溃将地球文明推向终点。为了让人类继续存在，一群幸存者秘密发起“启航计划”，建造启航舰，并尝试用尚未成熟的虫洞技术离开太阳系。尽管成功概率渺茫，但是计划最终成功：启航舰穿越虫洞，经过数年航行，抵达一颗陌生行星。飞船在降落时坠毁，但约一万人幸存，并得到当地智慧生命精灵的救援。人类随后将这颗星球命名为“启航星”。五位领导者使这场几乎没有成功可能的逃亡成为现实，也因此在第一代幸存者中获得了极高的威望，他们后来被共同称为——先行者。
迪崇是启航计划的总工程师，负责启航舰的整体设计、工程统筹与硬件架构。他将塞斯提出的核心技术与林内亚设计的生命维持系统整合进同一艘飞船，使不同领域的成果最终成为完整的工程结晶——启航舰。迪崇对设计与施工质量有近乎苛刻的要求，同时性情热情，善于以幽默缓解长期建设中的紧张气氛。严谨的工程标准与鲜明、开朗的个人气质，使他成为启航计划中最具个人魅力的领导者之一。

塞斯是启航计划的核心物理学家，负责关键技术研究，并主导实验性虫洞技术的开发。飞船建成后，他继续承担理论分析、航线计算与导航工作。塞斯性情冷静，言语简洁，习惯依靠计算、证据与逻辑形成判断。他很少轻易改变已经确认的结论，这种固执使他能够长期坚持艰难的科研方向，也使他在意见冲突中显得格外强硬。虫洞既是启航计划赖以成立的核心技术，也逐渐成为整个计划的象征，甚至被采用为计划的标志。多数普通成员无法真正理解塞斯的研究，因此对他始终存在一定距离感；但所有人都知道，人类能够离开太阳系，与这个沉默的物理学家直接相关。
启航舰尚未完成时，它就已经成了末日地球上值得发动战争争夺的东西。工程团队面对的不只是技术问题，还有军阀、恐慌、资源冲突，以及越来越接近崩溃的社会秩序。炽洛负责处理这一切。
炽洛是启航计划的政治家。飞船建设期间，他负责带领军队抵御试图夺取启航舰的军阀，并在战争、资源短缺和长期心理压力下维持建设体系的正常运转；航行开始后，他继续负责飞船社会的管理。炽洛自信，责任感强，善于组织人员、明确目标并在危机中迅速作出决策。他给民众带来的是末日从来没有的安全感，这也使许多人对他的判断保持很高的信任，而这种信任后来成为他政治力量的重要基础。
林内亚是启航计划的生物学家，负责医疗体系、维生系统与生态循环设计。启航舰无法无限携带空气、水和食物，因此生态循环能够维持多久，直接决定了飞船能够航行多久。林内亚也是计划中少数直接以“生命本身”为工作对象的技术负责人。她拥有高度专业化的背景，却没有技术官僚式的作风；即使在计划最紧张的时期，仍保持温和、开放的态度。

启航计划需要的资源规模远远超过一艘普通飞船，而计划实施时，地球原有的经济、工业和供应体系正在战争中瓦解。武器、设备、材料和生活物资仍然必须持续供应，否则再成熟的设计也只能停留在图纸上。海乐德是启航计划的经济学家，负责获取建设所需的武器、材料与物资，并在航行阶段管理生产和资源分配。她务实、独立，有很强的探索倾向，善于判断局势，也熟悉利益关系中的进退尺度。圆滑使她能够在不断变化的环境中与不同对象周旋，而审时度势则让她很少把某一种办法、渠道或关系视为永久可靠。普通成员对她的认识往往不像对炽洛那样直接，也不像迪崇的飞船那样具有明确的象征物；海乐德的作用更多隐藏在计划每天仍然能够获得材料、维持生产和继续建设这一事实之中。
五位先行者分别代表工程、科学、秩序、生命与资源。启航舰能够建成、离开地球、完成远航，并最终让人类在另一个世界重新建立社会，缺少其中任何一环都无法实现。对第一代幸存者而言，这些名字来自仍然鲜活的记忆：他们亲手将人类从旧文明的终点带到新文明的起点。

paragraphs: Project 1: Master Drawing Remix

The purpose of this project is for students to imitate a master's work to learn their techniques. Students need to incorporate a master's work into their drawing, add their own original elements, and keep the composition as harmonious as possible.
"A Faith Beyond Understanding" 22 × 33 inch Grey Rives BFK Paper, Black and White Charcoal

This artwork participated in the SCAD Foundation Studies Honors Exhibition 2026 and was selected as a finalist in the awards. This drawing incorporates Albrecht Dürer's "Praying Hands" and features a goat head drawn in an imitation of his style. I drafted it on grey paper using black and white charcoal. Meanwhile, the clothing patterns of the figure are inspired by traditional Tibetan attire; I attempted to use its rich decorative details and intricate patterns to add an exotic atmosphere to the composition.

During the conceptualization process, I strove to create an atmosphere where tranquility and unfamiliarity coexist, which is why I chose the elements in the composition: prayer, a goat, and ethnic minority clothing. The praying hands possess a sense of the sacred, while the goat is a symbol of the devil in Western culture, and the Tibetan clothing also carries an exotic vibe and a sense of the unfamiliar.

Secondly, in terms of composition, the goat head, the hands, and the clothing serve as focal points, forming a stable triangular structure. The goat's leftward gaze also guides the flow of the image, preventing the top-left corner from feeling empty. Drawing on grey paper better mimics Dürer's original work and effectively enriches the image.
At the same time, I also used color grading tools to create a color-graded version.
Project 3: Dramatic Mood Narrative

In this project, students are required to take a photograph with distinct light and shadow and a dramatic perspective angle, and then create a derivative work based on it, focusing on practicing perspective and the sense of lighting.
"Melancholy" 22 × 33 inch Blue Rives BFK Paper, Black and White Charcoal

This drawing primarily conveys an oppressive atmosphere. It uses a blue tone as the base and mainly relies on white for highlights. A major difficulty with this drawing is that the paper has high saturation and is inherently a mid-tone, while mixing white and black charcoal can make the image look muddy, leaving very little room for error when making corrections. My composition referenced a cinematic shot from "Requiem for a Dream."

RequiemforaDream.webp The upper half of this cinematic shot is enveloped in a black gradient, presenting an oppressive atmosphere. This method not only aligns with the theme of my drawing but also intensifies the "infinite" feel of the buildings in the frame.

paragraphs: 这个项目的目的是让学生模仿大师作品以学习其技法。学生需要在画面中使用一个大师作品，并原创自己的元素，并且让画面尽可能保持和谐。
《理解之外的信仰》 55.88×76.2cm灰色RivesBFK画纸 黑白双色炭条
这幅作品参加了SCAD的展览Foundation Studies Honors Exhibition 2026，并在评奖活动入围决赛。 这幅画结合了丢勒的《祈祷的手》，并模仿其风格绘制了羊头。我在灰色的纸张上起稿，使用了黑白炭笔。同时人物的服饰的纹样灵感来源于藏族传统服饰，我试图让其丰富的装饰细节和繁复的纹饰为画面增添异域感。
在创作的构思过程中，我力求营造一种宁静与陌生并存的氛围，也是因此我选择了画面中的元素：祈祷，山羊，少数民族服装。祈祷的手有一种神圣感，而山羊在西方文化中是恶魔的象征，藏族的服饰也有异域氛围和陌生感。
其次，在画面构图中，羊头，手，服饰分别作为画面焦点，构成了三角形的稳定构图。羊头向左的视线也引导画面走向，让画面左上角不显得空旷。而在灰色纸张上作画更好的模仿了丢勒的原作，也有效丰富了画面。
在这个项目，学生需要拍摄一个光影明显，透视角度大的照片，并对其进行二次创作，着重练习透视和光感。
《惆怅》 55.88×76.2cm蓝色RivesBFK画纸 黑白双色炭条
这张画主要表达压抑氛围。使用了蓝色调为基底，主要使用白色提亮。 这幅画非常大的难点就是纸张饱和度高而且本身就是中间色，而白色和黑色炭笔混合会让画面变灰，所以修改的容错很少。我的画面构图参考了《梦之安魂曲》的电影镜头
RequiemforaDream.webp 这个电影镜头的上半部分被黑色渐变笼罩，呈现出一股压抑氛围。这种方法不但契合我的绘画主题，而且可以让画面楼房的“无限”感更强烈。
同时，在我拍摄过程中也有额外产出：萨凡纳的教堂夜景。这个照片也很有氛围感，但是因为过于复杂，碳条很难表现细微细节，最终放弃。但是我仍然认为这是一个有意义的摄影作品。

paragraphs: FOUN 111 - Drawing and Painting Professor:

As a student with a prior background in drawing, the course material was relatively straightforward for me. However, it was precisely during this class that I developed the idea of building my personal website, and Professor Roberson give me help and support throughout the process.
FOUN 110 - Design: Thought and Process Professor:

In this course, I explored core design methodologies and mindsets, learning how to plan, structure, and execute creative projects. Additionally, I acquired foundational printmaking skills, learned the complete workflow of relief printing, and gained hands-on experience with essential Adobe creative tools, including Adobe Portfolio, Adobe Color, Adobe Express, and Adobe Illustrator.
Printmaking: "The Flow of Time"

Printmaking was an incredibly engaging experience. After iterating through several rounds of drafts, I began carving my block. My design was inspired by the Time Tunnel from Doraemon and the fluid, sweeping motion characteristic of Van Gogh's paintings.

The pattern is composed of three distinct layers: a woodgrain texture for the base, a swirling vortex in the middle, and a clock face on the top layer. A minor flaw occurred during carving where the number "10" was accidentally mirrored. This was primarily due to the preliminary sketch on the block becoming smudged and blurred over long hours of work.

Printing the blocks was equally fascinating. I mastered the entire process of inking, pressing, and cleaning the printmaking tools. If too little ink is applied, the print turns out faint and blurry; if too much is used, it bleeds into the carved grooves. Consequently, controlling the ink coverage is quite a delicate task for a beginner. After practicing with single-color prints, I experimented with printing using multiple colors.
Following the printing phase, I experimented with vectorizing my engraved artwork.
Spiked Tower Paper Model

Also in this course, I challenged myself to create a paper sculpture as an exploration into 3D design. In practice, planning an abstract model presents a high level of difficulty. Since the materials allocated to each student for this project were strictly limited, I had to minimize any material waste.

After completing the initial concept renderings, I thought a triangular tower would not be overly complex. However, when drafting the flat layouts on paper for cutting, I realized that producing a large number of precise prisms required highly accurate nets. Since drafting templates for irregular pyramids is exceptionally challenging, I ultimately adopted an iterative approach—cutting and defining the shapes simultaneously to resolve the template as I went.

花纹分为3层：底层是木纹花纹，中层是漩涡螺旋，顶层是时钟。美中不足的是，雕刻中数字10被刻反了，这主要是因为长时间工作让版面上的草稿模糊导致的。

同时在这节课，我尝试制作了一个纸雕塑。这是我对3D设计的尝试。事实上做一个抽象模型对于规划的难度很大，由于对于这个项目，每个人可以使用的材料是有限的，因此，我必须尽量减少材料浪费。
在我画完效果图后我本以为三角形的塔不会有非常大的难度，但是在纸张上绘画裁切图纸时，我发现想要制作出大量符合预期的棱柱体需要准确的图纸，而画不规则的棱锥的图纸事实上很难，最终我采取了边裁切边确定图纸形状的做法。

paragraphs: As an art student, I have been using Obsidian for note-taking for almost two years. Counting the time I spent experimenting with other note-taking tools before that, I have over four years of experience in total. During this time, I have tried almost every mainstream note-taking app, but in the end, only Obsidian stayed. The reason is simple—it allows me to fully control my knowledge and creative work.
I. The Limitations of Traditional Note-Taking Tools

If you are used to taking notes in Word or similar software, you have probably faced this problem: When the number of notes is still small, everything seems orderly; but once you accumulate dozens or even hundreds of files, no folder structure can help you quickly locate what you need.

This problem becomes especially serious when studying grammar, programming, or art theory. Knowledge points are often fragmented and interconnected, yet Word's linear file structure isolates every document, preventing cross-reference. For example, when I take notes on English grammar, I often recall related grammatical ideas. If I put everything into one document, the content becomes messy; if I split them into several files, it becomes hard to reconnect them when needed.

I once tried to build my original world-building notes using dozens of Word files. Years later, I realized I had written the same concept four or five times because I forgot which folder contained the original version. Whenever a new idea came up, I had to decide where to put it. This process was inefficient and broke my creative flow. Over time, the more notes I made, the heavier the burden became.
II. The Core Advantage of Obsidian: Connecting Everything
Obsidian completely changes this situation. Its bidirectional links allow your notes to connect with each other like Wikipedia, forming a living and expanding knowledge network.

You can break every tiny concept into a single note—even if it's just one or two sentences—and link them together to create a structured thinking system. This means you no longer depend on complex folder hierarchies to "find" your content, because everything is already interconnected.

When I write stories, I can instantly create a new note for each idea or character and add links to related concepts. Later, when I read the story, I can click the link to review or expand on those concepts immediately.

When I first discovered bidirectional linking, I decided almost instantly to migrate all my notes to Obsidian—even though I didn't yet fully understand Markdown syntax. At that moment, I realized that this flexible, interconnected way of working was exactly what I had been searching for.
This transformation—from static documents to a dynamic network—is the true reason I abandoned Word and fully adopted Obsidian.
III. Freedom and Control

paragraphs: 作为一名艺术学生，我使用Obsidian做笔记已经快两年了。算上之前尝试其他笔记工具的时间，总共有超过四年的经验。 在这段时间里，我几乎尝试过所有主流的笔记应用，但最终只有Obsidian留了下来。原因很简单——它让我能够完全控制我的知识和创作工作。
如果你习惯在Word或类似软件中做笔记，你可能遇到过这个问题： 当笔记数量还很少时，一切看起来井井有条；但一旦积累了几十甚至上百个文件，再复杂的文件夹结构也无法帮你快速定位所需内容。
这个问题在学习语法、编程或艺术理论时尤其严重。知识点往往是碎片化且相互关联的，但Word的线性文件结构将每个文档隔离开来，无法实现交叉引用。 例如，当我记录英语语法笔记时，我经常会想起相关的语法概念。如果我把所有内容放在一个文档里，内容会变得混乱；如果我把它们分成几个文件，需要时又很难重新连接它们。
我曾经尝试用几十个Word文件构建我的原创世界观笔记。几年后，我意识到我把同一个概念写了四五遍，因为我忘记了哪个文件夹包含原始版本。每当有新想法时，我都要决定把它放在哪里。 这个过程效率低下，打断了我的创作思路。随着时间推移，笔记越多，负担就越重。
Obsidian完全改变了这种情况。 它的双向链接让你的笔记像维基百科一样相互连接，形成一个活跃且不断扩展的知识网络。
你可以把每个微小的概念都拆分成单独的笔记——即使只有一两句话——然后将它们链接在一起，创建一个结构化的思考系统。 这意味着你不再依赖复杂的文件夹层次结构来"查找"内容，因为一切都已经相互连接了。
当我写故事时，我可以立即为每个想法或角色创建一个新笔记，并添加相关概念的链接。之后，当我阅读故事时，我可以点击链接立即回顾或扩展这些概念。
当我第一次发现双向链接时，我几乎立刻决定将所有笔记迁移到Obsidian——尽管当时我还不完全理解Markdown语法。 在那一刻，我意识到这种灵活、相互连接的工作方式正是我一直在寻找的。
这种转变——从静态文档到动态网络——是我放弃Word并完全采用Obsidian的真正原因。
大多数笔记工具将你锁定在它们自己的生态系统中。 它们要么限制导出选项，只允许部分内容导出，或者更糟的是，将你的数据加密并绑定到它们的云端，使迁移变得困难。
Obsidian采取了相反的方式。 你的所有笔记都以纯Markdown文件的形式存储在本地。你可以用任何文本编辑器打开、编辑、同步和备份它们。 你的数据真正属于你。
此外，Obsidian的所有本地功能都是完全免费的，这使它成为学生和独立创作者最具性价比的选择之一。
